name: שֶׁלַח
summary: Shelah son of Arpachshad, the grandson of Shem, and father of Eber, from whom the Hebrews are named: in the line from Shem to Abram (Gen 10:24; 11:12–15; 1Ch 1:18, 24) and so in Luke's genealogy of Jesus (Luk 3:35, Σαλά). He was born when Arpachshad was thirty-five, fathered Eber at thirty, and lived four hundred and three years after. The name is spelt as the noun שֶׁלַח, in pause שָׁלַח: “weapon” (2Ch 23:10), or in its other use what is put forth, a shoot (Sng 4:13). Scripture does not explain it, so which the name meant is not shown.

evidence.note: “Arpachshad fathered שָׁלַח, and שֶׁלַח fathered Eber”: the name in its pausal and its plain form in one verse.
Arpachshad lived thirty-five years and fathered Shelah; Shelah lived thirty years and fathered Eber, and after that four hundred and three years.
“Of Eber, of Sala (Σαλά; Peshitta שָׁלָח)”. Luke's list has a Cainan between Shelah and Arpachshad (verse 36), whom the Hebrew of Genesis does not name.
The noun the name is spelt as: “each man with his weapon (שִׁלְחוֹ) in his hand.”
The noun's other use: “your shoots (שְׁלָחַיִךְ) are an orchard of pomegranates.”

note: Nine uses (Gen 10:24 twice; 11:12, 13, 14, 15; 1Ch 1:18 twice; 1:24); the brief's 77 for v.dl.ac are mostly the verb שָׁלַח, spelt like the name's pausal form. Not to be confused with Judah's son שֵׁלָה (Shelah@Gen.38.5), spelt with ה and of another root. TIPNR's summary calls him “a son of Cainan”, following Luk 3:36; the Hebrew has Arpachshad as his father. The name could also be read “sent” or “a sending” from the verb; the entry keeps to the noun the spelling matches.
